acceptance_criteria.criterion: Health is fetched in parallel for all initialized workspaces.
A warning badge with issue count appears for workspaces with health issues.
No badge appears for healthy or uninitialized workspaces.
Health fetch failures do not break the workspace table rendering (graceful degradation).
All dynamic strings rendered via textContent.

summary: Added `wsHealthMap` object alongside `wsStatusMap` in `renderProjectDetail`, fetching workspace health for all initialized workspaces in parallel using `Promise.all([Promise.allSettled(...status), Promise.allSettled(...health)])`.
Health fetch failures are captured as `null` (same pattern as status), satisfying the graceful-degradation AC.
Updated `buildWorkspacesSection` signature to accept `wsHealthMap` as 4th parameter.
Added a 'Health' column header to the workspace table.

Added a health cell per row: shows a `.health-badge` with ⚠ icon and issue count only when `ws.initialized && healthReport.issues.length > 0`; renders an empty cell for uninitialized workspaces and healthy workspaces.
All badge text rendered via `textContent` (AC5 satisfied).
All 699 existing tests pass.

comments.note: `buildWorkspacesSection` now has a 5th parameter `wsHealthMap` between `wsStatusMap` and `onRefresh`. This is a positional-argument function — if any caller outside this file were to call it, the extra parameter would silently break it. Not a current issue (function is private to the module), but worth noting if this section is ever refactored.

The health icon uses raw Unicode '\u26a0' (⚠) via textContent. Consider replacing with an SVG or a dedicated icon component consistent with the edit-icon button approach used elsewhere in the project (e.g., in buildMetaSection).
No observations beyond the above — project-detail.js is well-structured and the health fetch mirrors the existing status-fetch pattern cleanly.

summary: Reviewed gui/public/js/views/project-detail.js against all four review dimensions. Clean PASS with no blocking issues.

Parallel fetch implementation: Promise.all([Promise.allSettled(statusFetches), Promise.allSettled(healthFetches)]) is the correct pattern — all N status and N health requests fire simultaneously, individual failures captured as null without blocking the view render.

Health badge logic: ws.initialized guard is correct (uninit workspaces can't have health reports). Badge condition is fully defensive: null-check, healthy flag, Array.isArray, length > 0. No false positives possible.

aria-hidden='true' on the warning icon is correct accessibility practice. All text via textContent — XSS clean.
